steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Cream butter and confectioners' sugar together in a large bowl. Beat in egg, vanilla, and almond extract.
Whisk flour, baking soda, and cream of tartar together in a medium bowl. Add to butter mixture; beat until dough is just combined. Divide dough into thirds and shape each portion into a ball.

Place one portion of dough on a lightly floured surface and roll out to 1/4-inch thickness. For each sandwich cookie, cut out two 3-inch hearts; cut out the center of one of the hearts with a 1 1/2-inch cutter. Place cutout pieces 1 to 2 inches apart on an ungreased cookie sheet. Repeat with remaining dough.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly browned, 7 to 8 minutes. Cool completely on wire racks.
Frost each solid 3-inch cookie with Pink Valentine Frosting and top with an open-centered cookie to form a sandwich. Frost the remaining small hearts and serve as separate cookies.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Valentine Sandwich Cookies
raw_recipe.description: Perfect for Valentine's Day, these cute heart-shaped sandwich cookies with pink frosting feature a small heart-shaped cutout in the top cookie to reveal the filling inside.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Valentine Sandwich Cookies

review.reviewBody: I made over 400 Valentine Sandwich cookies for my dessert business clients this year using this recipe. I personally don't like crisp/cut-out sugar cookies, but everyone went NUTS over these cookies. My niece has me make them for softball games, parties, etc.--she loves them. After making so many of these, I can offer a few suggestions: (1) refrigerate dough for 2-3 hours (I made over 30 batches of dough & often let it refrigerate overnight). I always put the dough back in the refrigerator between batches. (2) I used 2 tsp of vanilla & eliminated the almond extract. (2) When I rolled out the dough, I used confectioners' sugar (10X) NOT flour--I even re-used previously roll-out dough without any problems. The confectioners' sugar gives the cookie a little extra flakiness. (3) I sprinkled colored sugar on the cookie with the cut-out section before baking-the colored sugar looks nice with the contrast of the frosting coming through the cut-out. (4) I baked the cookies on Silpat, but parchment would work too. (5)I used a different frosting: 2 cups confectioners' sugar (10X), 3/4 tsp vanilla and 4-6 tbsp half & half or whole milk, plus food coloring. The frosting was always a big hit. (6) I individually bagged the cookies in cellophane cookie bags & everyone commented on how freshed they stayed. I will be using this recipe for St. Patrick's with shamrock cookie cutters; green sugar & green frosting! Thanks for the recipe!

These were great. I didn't use frosting but used seedless raspberry jam in between the layers. I sprinkled powdered sugar on the side that was cut out before I sandwiched them together so I didn't get the sugar on the jam. Very pretty and quite a good cookie. The dough was a bit crumbly but I had made the mistake of putting it in the fridge for about 1/2 hour. It didn't need any refrigeration and I was able to knead the dough a few times to help it hold together. Rolling and cutting out was a snap. This cookie did not need frosting! Will make again!

I made this with the full intention of doing the whole "sandwich" thing. Unfortunately my cookie cutters were kind of big and also a lot of the cutout hearts didn't match up well with the smaller hearts. So I decided to serve them as is, separately without frosting. The taste and texture was very good (I omitted the almond extract)... not a soft cookie but not super crunchy as long as you watch the baking time. I baked for about 7 minutes. I usually have a terrible, terrible time with sugar cookie dough being too sticky and impossible to roll out. However I followed suggestions of chilling the dough AND using confectioner's sugar to roll out as opposed to flour. It wasn't foolproof but it was a much better experience. I also divided the dough into thirds and colored one red and another pink. The cookies turned out well, I ended upw tih multicolored hearts, some with holes in the middle. I think this might be my next roll-out sugar cookie recipe. Remember to chill the dough and use confectioners sugar to "flour" the dough and your work surface. I handled the out of this dough and it didn't get tough or dry.

I have been searching for a while now for a cookie that my mum use to make for me to bring to school for valentines day. To make the cookie more like hers, I omitted the icing and used seedless raspberry jam and then afterwards drizzled have of them with white chocolate. I'm not sure if anyone else has suggested this....but instead of trying to fight to get the cookies up and keeping there shape, roll the dough out on parchment paper...cut...remove excess dough then put in the oven on a cookie sheet! Definelty will be making again!

I like the simple ingredients in this cookie. The recipe doubles well. I refrigerated too long which was a pain, I rolled in icing sugar. Frosted with "All Natural Pink Frosting" coloured and flavoured with strawberries. Who needs artificial anything! The cookies and cut outs only need 4-5 minutes. Thank you!

First, let me say my review is based on the dough, only. My son and I made the dough to use for cut-out sugar cookies. That being said, this is THE BEST recipe I have EVER used. I attempt sugar cookies at Christmas every year, and this year, I found success! I made very few changes. I used the full amount of vanilla plus a full tsp of almond extract. I have used the dough both chilled and unchilled, and it is easier to roll if chilled first. Still, I only chilled it about 45 minutes, and it never went back into the fridge after that, but was still a dream to work with. I used powdered sugar to roll it out, and greased my cookie sheets. Exactly 6 minutes worked perfectly in my oven. This recipe is so good that my son and I are making them again today!

I omitted the almond extract and used 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract instead. I chilled the dough for 2 hours before cutting out hearts with star-shaped centers. The cookies do spread quite a bit in the oven so make sure to place them far apart on the cookie sheet. I made my cookies larger so I ended up baking them for about 10-12 minutes. I spread strawberry jam on half the cookies and sprinkled confectioners' sugar on the other half before sticking them together to make a sandwich. The cookies look so pretty and taste wonderful. Perfect for Valentine's Day! I will definitely be using this recipe again and again.

This is indeed a great sugar cookie recipe. BEWARE though, the icing recipe is too salty.. only add 1/8 tsp rather than 1/2.. i'm not even sure you need salt. It was easy to prepare.. make sure your dough is cold before rolling out to cut. (a couple of hours in the fridge beforehand)

I made this recipe today for Valentine's Day tomorrow. I like to make little treats for my husband to take to his co-workers. For a surprise, I used raspberry jalapeno jelly on the inside of the cookie sandwich! The outside I iced with a simple powdered sugar and milk icing. I found 8 minutes to be the perfect baking time for me. I stuck the dough in the freezer for a short wait on getting started with rolling and cutting. Per another user's advice, I rolled the cookies with powdered sugar instead of flour--unless you like extra sweet cookies, I'd recommend using the flour instead. A tasty cookie! Didn't have trouble with it running while baking :)

Definitely more flour is needed for the dough to be pliable and not sticky. I used 400gr at least. Instead of baking soda and cream of tartar, I used 1 tsp of baking powder and 1/2 tsp of salt. I followed the "Sugar Cookie Icing" and the result was awesome!

Delicious cookies - very light and buttery. The dough isn't as easy to work with as I thought is would be. That is until I got the hang of it by rolling between two pieces of lightly floured wax paper and putting it into the freezer - then doing the cut outs. I baked it on parchment paper and did sandwich cookies with seedless strawberry jam then gave the cookies a nice sprinkle of powdered sugar.
A great cookie, BUT... the ingredients don't call for the filling? Hmmm. I used seedless Raspberry. You will need about a small jar. Also, no recipe for the frosting.
This recipe was good I ended up putting too much jam. I suggest icing and putting the jam on over a pan and letting it dry there.
I liked it, but the dough was a little dry and brittle to work with. Might add a bit more butter next time.

I'm not a huge fan of sugar cookies but my family and coworkers loved these cookies! I melted some pink candy melts and iced the tops of some of them with that to make it easy. I also cheated and bought a bag of white cookie icing and decorated with that and then red/white sprinkles. I felt thicker than a quarter inch dough needed more like 8-9 min in the oven.
These were real good, very tender and crisp. I put pink sprinkles over the top cookies and small ones, and spread raspberry jelly between the top and bottom cookie.
I've made these just as sugar cookies several times. Everyone always loves the taste of these sugar cookies.
i loved that recipe! instead of sandwich cookies i made regular cookies instead but i still used this recipe! it was soooooo good!
I used the cookies as single layer and it is so tasty! My family and my son's classmates like it and said it is so good! Thanks for sharing this recipe, good job guys!

Used this recipe for Christmas cut out cookies. Very easy to work with dough. cooks up fast and delicious flavor. did add the almond extract. nice, soft cookie that tastes like one from a bakery. very pleased. will be our go to recipe for sugar cookies. want to also try with lemon extract next.
